items.context: @matthewbarby (25.416 seguidores, cuenta mediana), en inglés: BTC está por cerrar su 2.ª racha de 8 semanas en rojo desde 2014 (la anterior fue mayo de 2022); compara con la caída de 2022 (Fed, Luna) y apunta a acumular entre 52k y 47k. ~25 min, 3 respuestas, 188 vistas. Caídas y ciclos: se aporta con datos del Cycle Clock y del Drawdown Atlas.
items.suggested_text:
Weekly losing streaks say more about how the selling happens than about how deep it goes. The deepest drawdowns in $BTC history were in a different league: 2011 bottomed at -92.7% and took 622 days to reclaim its peak, 2013 went to -84.5% and needed 1,177 days. And 2013 alone shows how wide the range is: one of its two tops was recovered in 210 days, the other in 1,177.

What usually separates those outcomes isn't the trigger itself (a 50bps hike, a Luna) but how much leveraged and weak-handed supply still has to clear, and time under water is mostly the measure of that. A streak ends on a weekly close; a bottom tends to end when the people who had to sell are gone. Those two clocks rarely tick at the same speed.
